Thermal comfort in Europe · 2020–2024Code on GitHub ↗

Sources and calculation

What is measured?

One daily high temperature per grid cell. These fields are estimated from weather station observations. Grid resolution does not imply a station at every point.

Comfort score

100 − max(minimum − Tmax, 0) − max(Tmax − maximum, 0)

The period score is the sum of scores for all 1,827 days in 2020–2024, divided by 1,827. Individual years use all days in that year. Fractional degrees retain their fractions; scores are not capped at zero.

Comfortable days per year

Counts days with minimum ≤ Tmax ≤ maximum. For 2020–2024, the total is divided by five years. For example: 400 days in range over five years = 80 days per year. An individual year shows its actual count.

Your chosen range

Limits can range from −30 to 50 °C in whole degrees. Both measures are recalculated in your browser from counts and sums of the original temperatures. Fractional temperatures are preserved. The score is not calculated from the average temperature.

Sources and resolution

E-OBS v33.0e / KNMI / Copernicus / ECA&D: 0.1° grid, about 11 km from north to south. NOAA CPC / NOAA PSL: original 0.5° grid in eastern gaps, interpolated for display. Interpolation does not add climate detail.

E-OBS uses station reporting days; NOAA uses 06:00–06:00 UTC. The two sources are not fully homogeneous. Coastlines and borders: Natural Earth, 1:10 million scale.

Calculation checks

Formula and inclusive endpoints; recalculation of all 1,827 original daily fields; comparison of every land cell with the site’s 12 numerical files. View the calculation audit.

Colours and coverage

Both views use the same palette. Scores range from 76 to 98 points; values outside that scale use the endpoint colours. Days range from 0 to 150 days/year; higher values use the final red. Scales stay fixed across years and temperature ranges to allow comparison.

Numerical coverage: 99.18% of land cells within the map. Grey indicates missing data. For coastal display, a nearby valid cell’s colour can extend up to 0.2°. The details panel identifies when a nearby cell is used.

The map includes Europe, Türkiye, Cyprus and the part of Russia within its bounds. It covers more than the European Union. Borders follow the cartographic dataset.

A non-commercial research and education project. E-OBS data are subject to the ECA&D/E-OBS data policy.

E-OBS: Cornes et al. (2018), doi:10.1029/2017JD028200. Additional data: NOAA CPC / NOAA PSL, Boulder, Colorado, USA. Natural Earth cartography is in the public domain.
